## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(k\log\log k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Take both endpoints of a maximal matching to obtain a vertex cover X with |X| ≤ 2k in polynomial time.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O_q(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O_q(\lvert V\rvert k^q+k^2+k)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $\max\{q,2\}$ |

## Derivation

1. Use one-hot color variables $z_{x,c}$ only for x in X. Impose exactly one allowed color and properness inside G[X].

2. For v outside X, failure to extend means every color in L(v) occurs on a neighbor in X. Enumerate one witness neighbor u_c for every c in L(v) and forbid that assignment with $\bigvee_{c\in L(v)}\neg z_{u_c,c}$. An empty list gives an immediate NO.

3. There are polynomially many clauses for fixed q, width at most max(q,2), and O_q(k) variables. Outside vertices are independent, so nonfailure at each of them is sufficient to extend the coloring.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- A supplied optimal vertex cover is unnecessary.
- Counting satisfying assignments of this CNF counts extendible colorings of X, not all colorings of the original graph.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
